readme:
## README.md
# Bio-ORACLE v3.0 — Global Marine Environmental Layers

Global marine environmental rasters from [Bio-ORACLE](https://bio-oracle.org/) version 3.0,
converted to cloud-optimized GeoTIFF and aggregated to H3 hexagonal cells at **resolution 6**.

This bucket holds the **2010-decade baseline, depth-mean realm**: 16 requested layers, published
as 18 datasets (current direction and aspect are each split into a sine and a cosine component,
see [Circular layers](#circular-layers-current-direction-and-aspect)).

## Citation

Both papers must be cited:

> Assis, J., Fernandez Bejarano, S.J., Salazar, V.W., Schepers, L., Gouvea, L., Fragkopoulou, E.,
> Leclercq, F., Vanhoorne, B., Tyberghein, L., Serrao, E.A., Verbruggen, H., De Clerck, O. (2024)
> Bio-ORACLE v3.0. Pushing marine data layers to the CMIP6 Earth system models of climate change
> research. *Global Ecology and Biogeography*. https://doi.org/10.1111/geb.13813

> Tyberghein, L., Verbruggen, H., Pauly, K., Troupin, C., Mineur, F., De Clerck, O. (2012)
> Bio-ORACLE: A global environmental dataset for marine species distribution modelling.
> *Global Ecology and Biogeography*, 21, 272-281. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1466-8238.2011.00656.x

**License:** Bio-ORACLE is released under the GNU General Public License
([source](https://bio-oracle.org/downloads-to-email.php)). No version is stated upstream, so the
STAC `license` field is `other` with a link to the provider's terms rather than a guessed SPDX id.

## Layers

Water-column layers are the **depth-mean** realm (averaged over the water column), baseline
experiment, decade 2010. Terrain layers are **benthic** and static.

| Dataset | Column | Quantity | Units |
|---|---|---|---|
| `depthmean/thetao-mean` | `thetao_mean` | Sea water temperature | degrees C |
| `depthmean/so-mean` | `so_mean` | Salinity | PSU |
| `depthmean/sws-mean` | `sws_mean` | Current velocity | m/s |
| `depthmean/swd-mean-sin` | `swd_sin` | Current direction, sine component | dimensionless |
| `depthmean/swd-mean-cos` | `swd_cos` | Current direction, cosine component | dimensionless |
| `depthmean/no3-mean` | `no3_mean` | Nitrate | mmol/m3 |
| `depthmean/po4-mean` | `po4_mean` | Phosphate | mmol/m3 |
| `depthmean/si-mean` | `si_mean` | Silicate | mmol/m3 |
| `depthmean/o2-mean` | `o2_mean` | Dissolved oxygen | mmol/m3 |
| `depthmean/dfe-mean` | `dfe_mean` | Dissolved iron | mmol/m3 |
| `depthmean/phyc-mean` | `phyc_mean` | Primary productivity (phytoplankton carbon) | mmol/m3 |
| `depthmean/ph-mean` | `ph_mean` | pH | pH units |
| `terrain/bathymetry-mean` | `bathymetry_mean` | Mean depth, negative below sea level | m |
| `terrain/slope` | `slope` | Sea floor slope | degrees |
| `terrain/aspect-sin` | `aspect_sin` | Aspect, sine component | dimensionless |
| `terrain/aspect-cos` | `aspect_cos` | Aspect, cosine component | dimensionless |
| `terrain/tpi` | `topographic_position_index` | Topographic position index | m |
| `terrain/tri` | `terrain_ruggedness_index` | Terrain ruggedness index | m |

Each dataset publishes two assets:

```
public-bio-oracle/<prefix>/<name>/<name>-cog.tif              # WGS84 float32 COG, 7200 x 3600
public-bio-oracle/<prefix>/<name>/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet     # H3 res 6, hive-partitioned
```

## Query with DuckDB

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
INSTALL h3 FROM community; LOAD h3;

-- Temperature and oxygen for every ocean cell, joined on h6
SELECT t.h6, t.thetao_mean, o.o2_mean
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-bio-oracle/depthmean/thetao-mean/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') t
JOIN read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-bio-oracle/depthmean/o2-mean/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') o
  USING (h6)
LIMIT 10;
```

Build a full SDM covariate table by joining the layers you need on `h6`. Every dataset shares the
same cell set, so the joins are exact.

## H3 resolution: this data has no `h8` column

**This is deliberate, not a defect.** The source grid is 0.05 degrees (~5.5 km), so one pixel
covers ~31 km2. An h6 cell is 36.1 km2, which matches the pixel. An h8 cell is 0.74 km2, which
would replicate each measured value across ~42 identical cells and publish apparent detail the
source does not have.

To join against an h8-native dataset (GBIF or OBIS occurrences, carbon, GHS-POP), roll **that**
dataset up to h6:

```sql
SELECT h3_cell_to_parent(h8, 6) AS h6, COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-gbif/.../hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
GROUP BY 1
```

Columns present: `h6` (native), `h5`, `h0` (partition key).

## Aggregation

Every value is an **area-weighted mean** of the source pixels inside the cell. The columns are
already averages, so combining cells means averaging again, weighted by cell area, never adding.
There is no meaningful catalog-wide `SUM` of any column here.

These are raster reductions rather than feature conversions, so there is no `_cng_fid` column;
every row is one distinct cell and no de-duplication is needed.

## Circular layers: current direction and aspect

`swd` (current direction) and `aspect` are compass bearings in 0-360 degrees. **A bearing cannot
be averaged arithmetically** — two north-facing cells at 1 and 359 degrees would average to 180
degrees, due south. Each is therefore stored as its sine and its cosine, averaged independently,
and recombined on read:

```sql
SELECT s.h6,
       (degrees(atan2(s.swd_sin, c.swd_cos)) + 360) % 360 AS current_bearing_degrees,
       sqrt(s.swd_sin * s.swd_sin + c.swd_cos * c.swd_cos) AS directional_consistency
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-bio-oracle/depthmean/swd-mean-sin/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') s
JOIN read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-bio-oracle/depthmean/swd-mean-cos/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') c
  USING (h6)
```

`directional_consistency` is 1 where a single source pixel contributed and falls below 1 where
pixels within the cell pointed in different directions.

The same applies to `terrain/aspect-sin` and `terrain/aspect-cos`.

## No-data

The COGs use **NaN** as no-data rather than a numeric sentinel. `bathymetry_mean` reaches about
-10700 m, so the conventional -9999 would fall inside the physically valid range of that layer and
could be read back as a real depth. The hex has no NULL values: land and no-data pixels simply
produce no cell.

## Provenance

Source NetCDF files, as delivered by the Bio-ORACLE download service, are retained under
`public-bio-oracle/raw/`. Conversion to COG and the sine/cosine decomposition are done by
`catalog/bio-oracle/scripts/netcdf_to_cog.py` in the `data-workflows` repo.
